towns.question: Share of valid votes cast at each town's polling stations, Knesset elections 21–25.
towns.source: Central Elections Committee locality results (files for Knesset 21–25), computed for this page
towns.note: Each list is shown under the name it ran with that year. URWP: Union of Right-Wing Parties (Jewish Home, Tkuma and Otzma Yehudit), April 2019. New Right: Naftali Bennett and Ayelet Shaked's list, April 2019. Yamina: the alliance of New Right, Jewish Home and National Union, headed by Ayelet Shaked in September 2019; in 2021, Naftali Bennett's list. UTJ: United Torah Judaism. Otzma: Otzma Yehudit running alone. RZ: the Religious Zionism joint list (Religious Zionism, Otzma Yehudit and Noam), 2021 and 2022. Jewish Home: Ayelet Shaked's list, 2022. In 2026 Religious Zionism runs with Zehut and Otzma Yehudit runs separately. Soldiers' and other envelope ballots are counted nationally, not by town. Files for earlier elections: media21–media24.bechirot.gov.il/files/expc.csv.

poll2026.title: National-religious voters' 2026 vote intention
poll2026.question: Vote intention among national-religious voters.
poll2026.source: Dialog for Ynet and Yedioth Ahronoth
poll2026.sample: 508 national-religious members of Dialog's online panel (484 asked again after the Religious Zionism–Zehut union); weighted by sex; margin of error 4.4 points
poll2026.note: A survey of voters who identify as national-religious, not a count of votes. Respondents described themselves as "national-religious stream" (50%), "religious Zionism" (33%) or "Torani-leumi" (Hardal, 17%). A further 2% named another party and 1% said they would not vote.

trust.title: Trust in institutions: national-religious and secular Jews
trust.question: Share expressing trust in each institution.
trust.source: Israel Democracy Institute, Israeli Democracy Index 2025 (Tables 2.4, 2.6, 2.11, 2.12, 2.18)
trust.sample: 1,205 Jewish respondents; the national-religious subsample is about 155, so its figures carry a wide margin
trust.note: IDI's national-religious category includes respondents who identify as Haredi leumi (Hardal).
